record.paper_title:
AIM Workshop “Pólya-Schur-Lax Problems: Hyperbolicity and Stability
Preservers” — A List of Open Problems
record.context_brief: Hurwitz stability and Horn-type stable polynomial completion
record.original_question: Determine whether every stable polynomial of the form det(A+i(xB1+yB2)), with A skew-symmetric and B1,B2 positive definite, is characterized by the stated parity condition, and determine necessary and sufficient conditions for real-rooted polynomials f,g,h with prescribed roots to arise as coordinate specializations of a homogeneous stable polynomial F(x,y,z).

evidence.quote: Problem 2 (S. Fisk). (i) is a Lax-type problem for (Hurwitz) stable polynomials while (ii) is a Horn-type problem for stable homogeneous polynomials.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A polynomial p(x,y) ∈ ℂ[x,y] is called (Hurwitz) stable if p(x,y) ≠ 0 whenever Im(x) > 0 and Im(y) > 0. A homogeneous polynomial F(x,y,z) ∈ ℝ[x,y,z] is called stable if F does not vanish on the open upper half-plane in each variable (equivalently, F is real-stable in the appropriate sense).

(i) (Lax-type problem.) Let A be a real skew-symmetric n×n matrix and let B₁, B₂ be real positive-definite n×n matrices. Show that the polynomial
   P(x,y) = det(A + i(xB₁ + yB₂))
is stable and that every monomial xᵃyᵇ appearing in P(x,y) has total degree a+b of the same parity as n (even if n is even, odd if n is odd). Conversely, determine whether every stable bivariate polynomial P(x,y) whose monomials all have total degree of a single parity matching some integer n admits a representation of the form det(A + i(xB₁ + yB₂)) with A real skew-symmetric of size n and B₁, B₂ real positive-definite of size n.

(ii) (Horn-type problem.) Determine necessary and sufficient conditions on three real-rooted univariate polynomials f, g, h ∈ ℝ[t] with prescribed real root multisets such that there exists a homogeneous stable polynomial F(x,y,z) ∈ ℝ[x,y,z] satisfying
   f(t) = F(t,1,0),  g(t) = F(0,t,1),  h(t) = F(1,0,t).
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open problem at an AIM workshop. Recent work on determinantal representations of strictly Hurwitz stable polynomials (e.g., arXiv:2411.17526) addresses related but distinct questions on tube-domain stability rather than the specific bivariate Lax-type characterization via det(A + i(xB₁+yB₂)) or the Horn-type compatibility question for stable homogeneous trivariate polynomials. No source verifies a complete resolution of either part.

status_evidence.snippet: Problem 2 (S. Fisk). (i) is a Lax-type problem for (Hurwitz) stable polynomials while (ii) is a Horn-type problem for stable homogeneous polynomials.

status_evidence.title: Strictly Stable Hurwitz Polynomials and their Determinantal Representations
status_evidence.snippet: Determinantal representation results for polynomials strictly stable on a tube domain; engages with generalized Lax conjecture but does not resolve Fisk's specific bivariate characterization.
status_evidence.claim: Recent related work does not resolve Fisk's specific Lax-type or Horn-type questions.
